items.title: Resurgent in April, can bulls defy 'Sell in May' maxim?
items.description: Indian stock markets may see continued gains in May. Investors should resist the urge to sell. While a repeat of April's strong rally is unlikely, key indices have historically performed well in May. Moderate, stock-specific moves are expected. Elevated oil prices and a strong dollar could limit significant upside.

items.title: Stock Radar: Down over 20% from highs! Jio Financial Services stock showing signs of bottoming out
items.description: Jio Financial Services has established a strong base above 220 and broken out of a two-month inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, signaling building bullish momentum. Experts suggest short-term traders with a high-risk profile can buy for a target of Rs 280 in the coming weeks.

items.title: Tax shadow over charitable trusts with 'profit' motive
items.description: Three top-notch hospitals in Mumbai and a famous international spiritual organisation-all functioning as charitable trusts-have been denied Income tax (I-T) exemption on the grounds that they were carrying out commercial activities.

items.title: Vodafone Idea shares in focus after govt cuts AGR dues by 27%. Time to buy?
items.description: Vodafone Idea shares are in focus after the government reduced AGR dues by 27% to Rs 64,046 crore, easing financial stress. The move, along with a structured repayment plan, has improved investor sentiment, with Citi issuing a bullish call, citing better prospects for fundraising and network expansion.

items.title: Buy, Sell or Hold: Morgan Stanley maintains buy on Lotak Bank; Goldman Sachs retail sell on Avenue Supermarts
items.description: Brokerages are selectively approaching the market. Morgan Stanley is positive on Kotak Mahindra Bank due to strong earnings and attractive valuations. They maintain a neutral stance on Hindustan Unilever despite steady demand. Goldman Sachs remains cautious on Avenue Supermarts, citing demand sustainability and valuation concerns. The focus is on earnings visibility and balance sheet strength.

items.title: MTAR Technologies and three other stocks hit 5-year swing high breakout
items.description: In the NSE list of stocks with a market cap over Rs 10,000 crore, four stocks witnessed a 5-year swing high at the close on April 30, suggesting bullishness in these counters, according to StockEdge.com’s technical scan data.A 5-year swing high represents the highest price a stock has reached within a five-year timeframe. This level acts as a significant resistance point where the price has historically struggled to move beyond. This occurrence may be seen as a bullish sign, indicating the potential for further upward movement in the stock. However, it is worth noting that this is different from a 5-year breakout, which occurs when a stock’s price surpasses a key resistance level that has held for five years.

items.title: CDSL shares in focus after Q4 net profit tanks 20% to Rs 80 crore, margins under pressure
items.description: CDSL reported mixed Q4 FY26 results with profit declining despite steady revenue growth and improved operating performance. Margins narrowed while total income saw modest gains. The company crossed a milestone in demat accounts, reflecting rising investor participation, and maintained a stable outlook amid volatility, with continued focus on technology and infrastructure investment.

items.title: Cemindia Projects among 5 stocks that closed above VWAP
items.description: On April 30, the closing prices of five stocks in the Nifty500 pack rallied over 2% relative to their VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price), and a shift above the VWAP suggests a potential bullish trend, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data.When the closing price rises above the VWAP, it signifies that the closing price is higher than the average price at which it was traded throughout the day, with the average being weighted by trading volume. This occurrence is often interpreted as a potential bullish signal by traders and investors. Potentially indicating positive sentiment in the market.

items.title: IIFL Finance among 4 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: Four stocks from the Nifty500 segment were identified in the RSI Trending Up scan on April 30 after gaining over 2%, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. “RSI trending up” indicates strengthening price momentum, which may signal potential upward movement and help traders spot buying opportunities.

items.title: Negative Breakout: These 8 stocks cross below their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, eight stocks' close prices crossed below their 200 DMA (Daily Moving Averages) on April 30, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data. Trading below the 200 DMA is considered a negative signal because it indicates that the stock's price is below its long-term trend line. The 200 DMA is used as a key indicator by traders for determining the overall trend in a particular stock. Take a look:

items.title: West Bengal, Tamil Nadu among 5 state election results today. 10 things stock market investors should track under volatility
items.description: Vote counting for assembly elections in West Bengal, Assam, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Puducherry begins today. Equity traders anticipate a volatile trading week. Early trends are expected within two hours, with clearer leads by late morning. Investors are advised to focus on broader macro signals beyond political headlines. Crude oil prices and foreign fund flows remain significant market drivers.

items.title: Bullish start likely for Dalal Street as GIFT Nifty advances 100 points
items.description: Indian markets opened weak on Thursday, experiencing a partial recovery but remaining in the red. Persistent FII outflows, a weak rupee, and elevated crude oil prices are expected to keep markets sideways. The India VIX rose, indicating increased market fear, while the rupee gained slightly against the US dollar.

items.title: Stocks in news: Kotak Mahindra Bank, DMart, Vodafone Idea, Nestle India, Coal India
items.description: Markets closed the week with modest gains amidst a volatile trading environment. Key domestic triggers include financial results from Kotak Mahindra Bank, DMart, and Nestle India, while global cues like crude oil prices and the rupee's movement will be closely watched. Vodafone Idea's AGR chapter closure and Coal India's production dip are also significant.

items.title: Short covering fuels April rally, stock-specific action to continue in May
items.description: Analysts are identifying stock-specific opportunities for May following April's short-covering rally.  Bullish bets include Sun Pharma, Adani Ports, ONGC, Sona BLW, Bharti Airtel, ITC, and Kotak Mahindra Bank, with specific price targets and stop-losses. Conversely, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles shows bearish sentiment with a potential downside target.

items.title: Pharma Q4 outlook mixed: Hospitals steady, generics face revlimid drag
items.description: Indian pharma and healthcare firms face a mixed March quarter. While hospitals anticipate steady growth, generic drugmakers grapple with lost Revlimid sales and pricing challenges. Lupin and Divi's are poised for strong performance, with Sun Pharma and Torrent showing resilience. Apollo Hospitals expects robust traction across its diverse segments.

items.title: Nifty may keep to 23,500–24,800 range amid high oil prices, war uncertainty
items.description: Nifty is expected to trade within a narrow range of 23,500–24,800 due to geopolitical tensions and high oil prices. Analysts suggest a mildly positive bias, with specific trading strategies and stock picks like ITC and Tube Investments recommended for potential gains.

items.title: Third party premiums take the wheel in motor cover growth
items.description: TP premiums rose 9.3% in FY26, compared with 9% growth in OD, taking overall motor insurance expansion to about 9% on an estimated base of ?1.08 lakh crore. This contrasts with FY24, when OD grew a stronger 17.4% against roughly 10% for TP, supported by robust vehicle sales and pricing improvements. In FY25, OD grew at 8.1% while TP grew at 7.8%. The latest shift comes despite no increase in regulated TP premium rates since the pandemic.

items.title: Bank, insurance regulators not inclined to allow commodity derivative investments: SEBI
items.description: India's markets regulator, SEBI, will not permit banks and insurance companies to invest in commodity derivatives, according to its chairman. While SEBI had previously explored enabling pension funds to trade commodities, a decision remains undisclosed. The announcement led to a decline in Multi Commodity Exchange of India shares.

items.title: Tamil Nadu election impact: Sun TV Network shares plunge 10% as Vijay’s TVK heads for big upset
items.description: Actor-turned-politician C Joseph Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) is poised to disrupt Tamil Nadu's long-standing Dravidian party dominance, leading in 108 seats. This unexpected surge has sent shockwaves through the political landscape, impacting established players like the DMK and AIADMK. Sun TV Network shares saw a significant dip amid these electoral trends.

items.title: Vedanta shares jump 8% after demerger. Should buy, sell or hold the stock?
items.description: Vedanta share price surged 8% after its demerger into four entities, with analysts highlighting improved business focus but increased concentration risks. Brokerages remain optimistic on upside potential, supported by strong Q4 earnings, while advising caution for new investors amid ongoing price discovery and evolving valuations of the separated businesses.

items.title: Equitas Small Finance Bank shares rally 7% on 5-fold jump in Q4 profit to Rs 213 crore
items.description: Equitas Small Finance Bank shares saw a significant 7% rise. This surge followed the bank's announcement of a substantial 406% increase in its fourth-quarter net profit for FY26. The lender's strong performance was attributed to business expansion and improved asset quality. Advances and disbursements also showed robust growth. The bank's profitability metrics improved, with net interest margin rising.

items.title: DMart shares fall 4% after Q4 results. What are Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, others saying?
items.description: DMart Share Price: Avenue Supermarts shares fell on Monday. The company reported a 19% rise in net profit and revenue for the March quarter of FY26. It also added 58 new stores, crossing the 500 DMart store milestone. Experts offer mixed views. Morgan Stanley and Motilal Oswal maintain positive ratings, citing store expansion and improving trends.

items.title: Unfazed by 670X P/E, retail investors add Eternal on dips for 2nd quarter as stock trades 30% off peak
items.description: Retail investors are showing confidence in Eternal, a food delivery and quick commerce firm. They are buying its shares on price dips, undeterred by a high valuation. This trend continues for the second quarter. Meanwhile, mutual funds are increasing their holdings, while foreign institutional investors are reducing theirs. The company has reported strong revenue growth and improved profitability.

items.title: Top Nifty50 stocks analysts suggest buying in this volatile week
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, is a comprehensive report that evaluates five key components of 4,000+ listed stocks – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum – to generate standardised scores. The simple average of the above-mentioned five component ratings is normally distributed to reach an average score.

items.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank shares tank 5% after Q4 results. What Morgan Stanley, Nomura, other brokerages are saying
items.description: Shares of Kotak Mahindra Bank fell despite posting a solid Q4FY26 performance, with net profit rising 13.3% YoY and NII up 8.1%. Asset quality improved, with both gross and net NPAs declining. Despite the positive results, the stock slipped, but Morgan Stanley remains bullish, maintaining an “Overweight” rating

items.title: Why is market rising today? Sensex surges 600 pts, Nifty above 24,150. West Bengal election trends among 5 factors
items.description: Indian stock markets surged on Monday, with Sensex and Nifty rising nearly 1% as investors closely assessed early trends in West Bengal and other state election results. Broad-based optimism saw major indices and sectors gain, though Kotak Mahindra Bank bucked the trend. Analysts suggest the election impact will be short-term.

items.title: MCX shares drop 3% after Sebi chief's comments on commodity derivatives. What spooked investors?
items.description: MCX shares fell after SEBI signalled that banks and insurers are unlikely to be allowed into commodity derivatives. SEBI chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator won’t push the proposal with Reserve Bank of India.

items.title: Stock picks of the week: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 31%
items.description: If there is no negative development over the next few days, there is unlikely to be pressure on a large part of the market. It is, in fact, likely that the Indian market will be part of any upmove that emerging markets may see if there is a decline in crude oil prices. Our selected stocks for today depict a strong upward trajectory in their overall average score which is based on five key pillars: Earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum. This implies that there has been a significant improvement in their market outlook in the given time frame.

items.title: FIIs raised stakes in 13 stocks for 4 straight quarters; 5 turned multibaggers. Do you own any?
items.description: Monitoring the investment activity of institutional heavyweights like Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) can be quite insightful, as their moves are typically backed by deep research and long-term conviction. Over the four quarters ending March 2026, foreign institutional investors steadily raised their holdings for four consecutive quarters in 49 stocks, each with a market capitalisation exceeding Rs 10,000 crore.From a price performance perspective, 29 stocks have generated double-digit gains over the past one year. Of these, 13 rallied sharply between 60% and 352%, while 5 emerged as multibaggers, more than doubling investor wealth within a year. (Data source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Valor Estate shares locked in 20% upper circuit. What’s behind the sharp surge today?
items.description: Valor Estate shares hit a 20% upper circuit after the Bombay High Court ruled in its favour in a long-pending Bhayandar land dispute. The verdict removes ownership uncertainty over a key land parcel, boosting sentiment. The company is now positioned to explore development and monetisation opportunities linked to the asset.

items.title: Maruti Suzuki, Bajaj Auto, other auto stocks jump up to 5% after strong April sales
items.description: Shares of automakers like Maruti Suzuki and Bajaj Auto rose after strong April sales data lifted sentiment. The gains pushed the Nifty Auto index over 1% higher, led by robust performance from key players.

items.title: West Bengal election results put these 43 stocks under spotlight. Will BJP's win be a trigger?
items.description: Early West Bengal election trends putting BJP ahead of TMC have pushed stocks like Bandhan Bank, CESC, and Berger Paints into focus. Investors are watching potential policy shifts, though analysts say the impact will be short-lived, with broader cues such as crude oil prices likely to drive overall market sentiment.

items.title: M&M Q4 preview: PAT to rise up to 48% YoY amid sequential setback; revenue to grow up to 24% on strong volumes
items.description: Mahindra & Mahindra is expected to post strong YoY growth in Q4FY25, with PAT rising up to 48% and revenue growing up to 24% on robust volumes. However, margin pressures and sequential decline in profitability remain concerns, as rising costs and EV mix weigh on performance across brokerages’ estimates.

items.title: BHEL shares soar 13% after Q4 net profit rockets 156% YoY to Rs 1,290 crore, revenue up 37%
items.description: BHEL Share Price: Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL) shares surged over 13% after reporting a robust March quarter with a 156% jump in net profit to Rs 1,290.50 crore. Revenue from operations also saw a significant 37% increase. The company also recommended a final dividend of Rs 1.40 per share for FY26.

items.title: Adani Power, Ports & Enterprises: Why Jefferies just raised their target prices on 3 Adani group stocks
items.description: Jefferies has raised target prices on Adani Power, Adani Ports and Adani Enterprises, maintaining ‘Buy’ ratings on strong operational performance, capacity expansions and improving realisations. Adani Ports saw EBITDA beat estimates, supported by higher domestic port realisations and upcoming capacity additions. The brokerage expects steady volume growth and strong EBITDA momentum across the Adani group.

items.title: Zen Technologies shares tumble 11% after Q4 profit plunges 69% YoY
items.description: Zen Technologies shares saw a sharp fall of 11 percent. This happened after the company reported a significant drop in its March quarter earnings. Net profit declined by 69 percent year-on-year. Revenue from operations also faced pressure, falling 45 percent. The company announced a final dividend of Re 1 per share. Its order book stood at Rs 1,336 crore.
